parts.what_was_built: In 1997 the Harappa Archaeological Research Project (HARP) cleaned out Wheeler's 1946 cutting HP XXX on the west side of Mound AB (HARP Trench 42) and found 'a massive mud-brick wall of Period 2' (Kenoyer and Meadow 2000: 56). The re-examination of 1997-98 found a substantial Early Harappan occupation deposit and 'An Early Harappan wall', lying below the level that Wheeler and Mughal had discussed, and established that 'The Harappan phase wall was actually built on top of the Early Harappan city wall' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2001, section 'Fortification Wall'). From this and the Mound E evidence HARP concluded that 'both Mound AB and Mound E saw the construction of mud brick revetment or 'city' walls sometime during Period 2' (Kenoyer and Meadow 2000: 56); later summaries describe the Kot Diji settlement as divided into two mounds, AB and E, 'each with a massive mud-brick perimeter wall' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2001, section 'Kot Diji Phase Developments'), and the Kot Diji site as 'encompassing two separately walled settlements (Mound AB & Mound E)' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2005: 224). Only a short length of this wall has been exposed, in the trench; its full circuit is not published.
parts.locator: kenoyer2000ravi p. 56; meadow2001recent3 (section 'Fortification Wall'); meadow2001recent2 (section 'Kot Diji Phase Developments'); meadow2005harappa p. 224
parts.excavator_basis: HARP's Period 2 range, 'ca. 2800 BC - ca. 2600 BC' (Kenoyer and Meadow 2010: xlv, Table 1), is given in 'approximate calendar years based on calibrated radiocarbon determinations' (xlv, n. 3), with periods defined by radiocarbon and by comparative analysis of pottery, architecture and other objects (xlv). The start of the phase is weakly dated: 'The beginning of the Kot Diji Phase (Period 2) remains largely undated at Harappa' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2005: 209), and Table 1 of that paper writes the range as 'c. 2800(?) - 2600/2500 BC' (p. 207). The wall is assigned to Period 2 by stratigraphy and associated Early Harappan pottery; no determination from its construction has been published.

syntheses.statement: Kenoyer reports that Mughal (1970: 127-130 and personal communication) reinterpreted Wheeler's section to propose that 'the earliest part of the massive mud-brick structure was constructed by the Early Harappan settlers', with Layer 26 the settlement before the wall and Layer 26A debris inside it (p. 38). Kenoyer adds that the earliest mud-brick in Wheeler's section 'may be correlated to the initial building of massive mud-brick walls as seen on Mound E during Period 2', i.e. that massive construction may have been under way on the west side of Mound AB at the same time as on Mound E (pp. 49-50). Period 2 here is the 1991 numbering, which falls within the later Kot Diji Phase (Period 2).
syntheses.disagreement: Disagrees with Wheeler (1947: 64, 93), for whom the defences were the first Harappan construction on the mound and post-dated the pre-defence occupation.

syntheses.statement: 'The original Ravi phase division into two settlements was maintained (Mounds AB and E), but during the Kot Diji phase these settlements appear to have been delimited by massive mud-brick perimeter walls'; the Kot Diji phase is Harappa Period 2, 2800-2600 BC.

In the Kot Diji Phase (2800-2600 BCE) the site covered about 27 hectares and 'the two different mounded areas were surrounded by massive mud brick walls'; the larger brick size (10 x 20 x 40 cm) 'was used for platforms and city walls'.

parts.conflicts: Wheeler (1947: 64, 93) took the fortification of Mound AB to mark the arrival of the mature Harappa culture, built over an 'alien' pre-defence occupation; Mughal (1970, via Kenoyer 1991: 38) argued that the lowest part of the mud-brick structure was Early Harappan, and HARP's 1997-98 work found an Early Harappan (Period 2) wall beneath the Harappan-phase wall. The radiocarbon evidence does not reach the nominal start of Period 2: the Period 2 determinations we found from Mound AB calibrate between 2857 and 2290 cal BC (excluding Beta-163712, which the authors reject as too late), and all four Period 2 ranges in Meadow and Kenoyer 2005 lie wholly or largely after 2600 cal BC, overlapping HARP's Period 3A. The 2005 attribution of those four samples to Mound AB rests on our lot-number inference.

parts.part: Mound AB (citadel): Harappan-phase fortification wall (Wheeler's defences)
parts.layout_phase: Period 3A (Harappa Phase A) in HARP's scheme; the first of Wheeler's three structural periods of the defences
parts.what_was_built: Wheeler's 1946 cuttings showed that 'After a preliminary occupation of the site or its vicinity ... mound AB was heavily fortified' and that 'the fortification marks the arrival of the mature Harappa culture' (Wheeler 1947: 64). The defences comprised a bund or 'rampart' 10-20 feet high of mud and debris with a mud-brick nucleus; on it a main mud-brick wall with a basal width of 40 feet and a height of upwards of 35 feet, revetted externally with baked brick; rectangular towers or salients; a co-eval internal platform of mud and mud-brick rising to 33 feet to carry the buildings of the citadel; a western gate-system with terraces; and three periods of construction, the original revetment being rebuilt after 'a long period of weathering' and later strengthened (pp. 64-65). HARP's re-examination of the HP XXX cutting found that this Harappan-phase wall was built on top of the Early Harappan (Period 2) city wall, 'was built up and refaced both inside and outside numerous times during the c. 700 years of the Harappan phase occupation', and that against its inner face 'The earliest street layers date to Period 3A and there is a continuous sequence through Period 3B and 3C' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2001, section 'Fortification Wall'). Kenoyer (2008, manuscript p. 13) summarises that at the beginning of the Harappa phase (Period 3A, 2600-2450 BCE) the division into two walled sectors was maintained and 'The Harappan city walls were constructed directly above or slightly offset from the Early Harappan walls'.
parts.locator: wheeler1947harappa pp. 59, 64-66; meadow2001recent3 (section 'Fortification Wall'); kenoyer2008urbanism manuscript p. 13
parts.excavator_basis: HARP: Period 3A is 'ca. 2600 BC - ca. 2450 BC' (Kenoyer and Meadow 2010: xlv), a range stated to rest on calibrated radiocarbon (xlv, n. 3; 'Based on radiocarbon determinations, we believe that Period 3A lasted from ca. 2600/2550 to ca. 2450 B.C.', Meadow and Kenoyer 1997: 140); the wall's attribution to the start of 3A is stratigraphic, from the earliest street layers against its inner face. Meadow and Kenoyer (2005: 209) place the transformation of the Kot Dijian into the Harappan at Harappa 'between c. 2600 and 2500 calBC, although, many more determinations are necessary to better date this process'. Wheeler gave no absolute date for the defences; he dated the mature civilisation by cross-dating with Akkadian contacts (Sargon 'now dated to c. 2350 B.C.') and proposed 'the millennium 2500-1500 B.C. as a possible inclusive date for the mature Harappa civilization' (Wheeler 1947: 78, 82).

syntheses.statement: The 1946 excavator's own estimate: 'the millennium 2500-1500 B.C. as a possible inclusive date for the mature Harappa civilization', resting on Akkadian cross-dating; the defences mark the arrival of that culture (p. 64).
syntheses.disagreement: Wheeler's 2500 BC lower bound is about a century later than HARP's radiocarbon-based start of Period 3A (c. 2600 BC), and Wheeler treated the defences as the first Harappan construction, whereas HARP found an Early Harappan wall beneath them.

syntheses.statement: Vats, who did not identify the fortification, dated Mound AB Strata I-IV (Late I-IV) as contemporary with the Late Period of Mound F (c. 2750-3050 B.C.) and Strata V-VI (Intermediate I-II) 'Before Circa 3050 B.C.', on the basis of comparison with Marshall's chronology for Mohenjo-daro.
syntheses.disagreement: Vats's levels are dated some 500-1000 years earlier than HARP's Harappan-phase periods; his scheme rests on cross-dating, not radiocarbon.

parts.conflicts: No radiocarbon determination has been published from Period 3A levels on Mound AB or from the construction of the wall; the phase immediately before (Period 2) is dated by the determinations listed under the previous part, and HARP's only Period 3A determination we found (Beta-163714) is listed under Mound E. The four Mound AB 'Period 3' dates of Kenoyer 1991 (WIS-2043, WIS-2144, WIS-2075, WIS-2140; p. 43) carry no sub-period and are not tied to the wall, so we leave them out. Wheeler's cross-dated 2500 BC and HARP's radiocarbon-based 2600 BC differ by about a century.

parts.layout_phase: Period 2 (Kot Diji Phase) in HARP's current scheme; in the 1991 scheme their construction opens Period 2 ('Early Harappan / massive mud-brick revetment walls', Kenoyer 1991: 40, Table 4.2)
parts.what_was_built: Excavations of 1988-1990 at the north-west corner of Mound E found 'at least five and possibly six different walls that are made of large mud-bricks (10 x 20 x 40 cm)' associated with Early Harappan ceramics; two are eroded and sealed by Early Harappan deposits, while 'the other three or four were built on the natural soil or by cutting foundation trenches into Early Harappan deposits' (Dales and Kenoyer 1991: 230). The most complete, wall #[164], runs for over 15 m, is 2 m wide and survives about 2 m high; wall #[235], built after it, is 2.5 m wide with a corner; both appear to be retaining or revetment walls (Kenoyer 1991: 47). Kenoyer (1991: 44) writes that 'The northwestern edge of this mound was eventually defined by the construction of a massive mud-brick wall or revetment', a change that defined the start of his Period 2. In Period 3 a thin baked-brick retaining wall (#[51]) and then a massive revetment (#[33]) were built over the edge (Dales and Kenoyer 1991: 235; Kenoyer 1991: 50). Kenoyer and Meadow (2000: 56) restate that 'The distinction between Periods 1 and 2 on Mound E was first defined by changes in the ceramic assemblage that coincided with the construction of a massive mud brick revetment wall along the northwestern edge of Mound E'.
parts.locator: dales1991summaries pp. 230, 235; kenoyer1991urban pp. 44, 47, 50; kenoyer2000ravi p. 56
parts.excavator_basis: The range is HARP's current Period 2 range (Kenoyer and Meadow 2010: xlv). The 1991 report dated its own Period 2 by radiocarbon: 'Period 2 dates are from upper stratigraphic levels ... These calibrated dates range from 2470 to 2405 BC (CALIB) and overlap with the dates of the following Period 3' (Kenoyer 1991: 38-39), and its single Period 1 hearth date calibrated 'to 3338, 3213, or 3203 BC' (p. 38). The later 2800-2600 BC range for Period 2 is not derived from these Mound E determinations, which fall later.

syntheses.statement: 'Based on a larger assemblage of ceramics and greater time depth, what we previously called Period 1 on Mound E should now be designated as late Period 1B (with some Period 1A sherds mixed in).' The pre-wall deposits on Mound E thus belong to the end of the Ravi Phase, and the walls to the start of the Kot Diji Phase.
syntheses.disagreement: Relabels the 1991 sequence (Dales and Kenoyer 1991; Kenoyer 1991), in which Period 1 was Early Harappan (Kot Dijian) and Period 2 'Transitional'.

syntheses.statement: Excavations of 1988-1990 at the north-west corner of Mound E 'revealed portions of the Harappa Phase city wall that surrounded Mound E and numerous mud-brick platforms', and the deepest levels 'revealed the presence of the Kot Diji Phase (now Period 2) occupation'.

On the western edge of Mound E, as on Mound AB, the Kot Dijian to Harappan transition shows 'strong continuities in settlement planning. The Harappan city walls were constructed directly above or slightly offset from the Early Harappan walls.'

parts.conflicts: HARP's period numbering changed twice. In 1991 Period 1 was the Early Harappan (Kot Dijian) occupation before the revetment walls and Period 2 the 'Transitional' deposits after them (Dales and Kenoyer 1991: 240; Kenoyer 1991: 38); after the Ravi Phase was found on Mound AB in 1996, the old Period 1 on Mound E became late Period 1B and Period 1 and 2 were renamed Ravi and Kot Diji (Kenoyer and Meadow 2000: 55, 58). Beta-33873 is therefore labelled Period 1 (1991), Period 1/2 (2000) and, by the text, late Period 1B. The 1991 Period 2 determinations from this corner calibrate to c. 2470-2405 BC by intercept and overlap Period 3 dates (Kenoyer 1991: 38-39), some 130-400 years later than the 2800-2600 BC range now given for Period 2, while the single pre-wall date falls in the late fourth millennium BC.

parts.part: Mound E: southern and eastern perimeter wall with the south gateway
parts.layout_phase: Period 3A (Harappa Phase A), 'at the very beginning of the Harappan phase'
parts.what_was_built: On the southern slope of Mound E (Area F) the 1990 season found two superimposed massive mud-brick walls. The earlier, #[40], was built directly on the gently undulating natural surface, its lowest courses stepped to the ground; its mortar contained Period 3 sherds and 'Other pottery found beneath the wall confirms that wall #[40] was built during Period 3'; it appears to have been free standing. After it had eroded, wall #[30] was built just inside its line, traced in an arc for over 73 m, 5.4-6.5 m wide and 8.5 m wide at gateway #[84], with evidence for an earlier entrance #[85] (Dales and Kenoyer 1991: 251); the entrance was 2.8 m wide and faced with baked brick (p. 256). Meadow and Kenoyer (1997: 140) date this 'massive mud brick city wall pierced by a gateway' to 'the very beginning of the Harappan phase in Period 3A along the southern edge of a Period 2 settlement now estimated to have covered the whole of Mound E'; in 1993 it was traced to a mud-brick bastion at the south-east corner, where it turns and is incorporated into the eastern edge of Mound E, and it was rebuilt at least once (perhaps at the start of Period 3B) and repaired at the start of Period 3C. On the east side the same circuit, Wall [250], c. 6 m wide, 'is thought to have been first constructed in Period 3A at or near the beginning of the Harappan Phase'; a deep sounding against its outer face found at least 3 m of Period 3A and 3B street deposits over 'about two metres of late Period 2/early Period 3A occupational debris and below that, natural sediment' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2000: 326). Kenoyer (2008, manuscript p. 13) contrasts this with the west side: 'On the eastern edge of Mound E, domestic structures were replaced by Harappan streets, and the Harappan city wall was constructed along a different plan.' On the southern slope Period 2 houses already stood along a major street marked by cart tracks cut into natural soil (Kenoyer 1991: 47).
parts.locator: dales1991summaries pp. 251, 256; meadow1997harappa p. 140; meadow2000tiny p. 326; kenoyer2008urbanism manuscript p. 13
parts.excavator_basis: The period range is radiocarbon-based: 'Based on radiocarbon determinations, we believe that Period 3A lasted from ca. 2600/2550 to ca. 2450 B.C.' (Meadow and Kenoyer 1997: 140); the 2010 chart gives 'ca. 2600 BC - ca. 2450 BC' (Kenoyer and Meadow 2010: xlv) and the 2005 chart 'c. 2600/2500 - 2450/2400 BC' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2005: 207). The wall's attribution to the start of 3A is stratigraphic and ceramic (Period 3 sherds in the mortar and beneath the wall, Dales and Kenoyer 1991: 251; Period 3A street deposits against Wall [250], Meadow and Kenoyer 2000: 326). No determination from the wall itself has been published.

The paper's 2000 work on Period 3A was in Trench 54 on the west side of Mound E (pp. 208, 214-215), and its figure captions place 2000 lots 2087-2342 there (Figs. 8 and 11); we assign the sample to Trench 54, Mound E West, by that inference. Trench 54 lies away from the southern and eastern wall, and the relation of the 'massive city wall' in nearby Trench 57 to the rest of the perimeter 'remains unclear' (p. 208).

syntheses.statement: HARP-based web summary: the original mud-brick perimeter wall found in 1990, about 5 m wide, was built on natural soil; 'No deposits of Period 1 (3300-2800 B.C.) were found. In some areas, this mud-brick wall cuts through deposits of Period 2 (2800-2600 B.C.) occupation. The wall is dated at the beginning of the Harappan phase occupation, or Period 3A (2600-2450 B.C.).' A second wall, 5 m wide, was built on top of it in Period 3B, and the first major repair dates to 3C.
At the south-east corner, 'The bastion area consists of a Period 3B (2450-2200 B.C.) wall built upon a Period 3A (2600-2450 B.C.) wall'.
The settlement 'grew to become a small town with two major walled areas by ca. 2600 BC' (the walled areas are Mounds AB and E).
The 1990 field report assigns wall #[40] to Period 3 (the Harappan phase) without sub-period, from Period 3 sherds in its mortar and beneath it.
syntheses.disagreement: Less specific than the later attribution to the very beginning of Period 3A (Meadow and Kenoyer 1997: 140).

parts.conflicts: The start of the layout phase is placed at c. 2600 BC (or 2600/2550 BC) by HARP's period charts, but the one Period 3A determination we found (Beta-163714, 2475-2285 cal BC) and the Period 2 and Period 2/3 determinations from Mound E, such as A-7527 (2575 (2464) 2320 cal BC), WIS-2218 (intercepts 2556-2493 BC) and WIS-2216 (2464 BC), fall after 2600 BC; Meadow and Kenoyer (2005: 209) themselves put the Kot Dijian-Harappan transition 'between c. 2600 and 2500 calBC' and call for more dates. The 1990 report assigns the southern wall to Period 3; from 1997 it is placed at the start of 3A. Whether the south and east wall had a Period 2 predecessor is not stated: the southern wall stands on natural soil and cuts Period 2 deposits, unlike the north-west corner and Mound AB, where Harappan walls sit on Early Harappan walls.

parts.part: Mound ET: perimeter wall and south-east gateway
parts.layout_phase: Early in the Harappan occupation of Mound ET, after ca. 2470 B.C. (Meadow and Kenoyer 1997); Period 3B in Kenoyer 2008
parts.what_was_built: A massive baked-brick gateway and drain complex at the south-east corner of Mound E is 'set between the southeastern corner of the mud brick city wall of Mound E and a similar mud brick city wall running along the southern edge of Mound ET'. 'The first gateway appears to have been constructed early in the occupation of Mound ET, when the already existing Mound E perimeter wall was extended to enclose Mound ET. Radiocarbon dates from a hearth directly beneath this new extension indicate that it was built sometime after ca. 2470 B.C.' Ceramics from early deposits inside the wall relate to Periods 3A and 3B; the second gateway phase is placed at the start of Period 3C (ca. 2250 B.C.) and the third at the end of 3C (ca. 2000 B.C.) (Meadow and Kenoyer 1997: 143-144). In Trench 22 'there were considerable deposits of cultural material at plane level prior to the construction of the Mound ET city wall', including agate and steatite working debris, and the wall was rebuilt two or more times (p. 147). Kenoyer (2008, manuscript p. 13) places the walling of this sector in Period 3B: 'During Period 3B, from 2450-2200 BCE, the city began to grow dramatically, with major walled suburbs constructed to the north and south of Mound AB, and to the east of Mound E.'
parts.excavator_basis: The terminus post quem of ca. 2470 B.C. is radiocarbon (A-8047 and A-8048 from a hearth beneath the wall, Meadow and Kenoyer 1997: 143); the 3A/3B ceramic attribution of the early deposits inside the wall is cross-dating by pottery (p. 144). The range [2450, 2200] is Kenoyer's Period 3B (2008, manuscript p. 13), the period to which he assigns the walled suburb east of Mound E; Meadow and Kenoyer (1997: 140) give 3B as 'ca. 2450 to ca. 2250 B.C.'.

syntheses.statement: HARP-based web summary: 'The gateway appears to have been built during the initial Harappan phase of Mound ET occupation, when an extension of the Mound E city wall was built to enclose Mound ET. Radiocarbon dating and ceramic analysis place this initial phase of construction during period 3A (2600-2450 B.C.) and 3B (2450-2200 B.C.).'
syntheses.disagreement: Allows construction in late Period 3A, whereas the 1997 report gives only 'sometime after ca. 2470 B.C.' and Kenoyer (2008) places the walled sector in 3B.

parts.conflicts: The 1997 report dates the Mound ET wall only by a terminus post quem (after ca. 2470 B.C., from two dates beneath it) and lists those dates under a Period 3B heading; the HARP 3-D site summary places the first construction in 3A and 3B; Kenoyer (2008) assigns the walled suburb east of Mound E to 3B. A-8049 from the same context is younger (intercepts 2195-2149 cal BC) and is flagged as somewhat aberrant.

parts.part: Mound F: perimeter wall and Great Hall ('granary')
parts.what_was_built: HARP's work on Mound F in 1996-2000 indicates that 'this part of the site was settled only during the middle of the Harappa Phase (Period 3B)': during the Kot Diji and Period 3A phases the area was mined for clay to build the walls and houses of Mound AB and then filled with garbage, and 'During Period 3B, beginning c. 2450/2400 calBC, we see substantial occupation of the area and the construction of a massive mud-brick perimeter wall' (Meadow and Kenoyer 2005: 211-212). The wall runs along the north edge of Mound F and 'probably articulates with a wall discovered along the western edge of the mound. In both areas the wall is over 14 meters wide and built up through several phases of construction'; at the Great Hall three building episodes were defined, the earliest a single wall below the Great Hall, then the Great Hall, then a platform carrying the Later Hall (Meadow and Kenoyer 2001, section 'Granary or Great Hall'). Kenoyer (2008, manuscript pp. 13-14) states that the 'granary' or 'Great Hall' 'was constructed at this time [Period 3B] in one of the new walled suburbs called Mound F' and was built 200 years before the circular brick platforms of Period 3C.
parts.locator: meadow2005harappa pp. 211-212; meadow2001recent4 (section 'Granary or Great Hall'); kenoyer2008urbanism manuscript pp. 13-14
parts.excavator_basis: Period 3B is 'ca. 2450 BC - ca. 2200 BC' (Kenoyer and Meadow 2010: xlv; 'c. 2450/2400 - 2200 BC', Meadow and Kenoyer 2005: 207), a radiocarbon-based period range. The attribution of the Mound F wall and Great Hall to 3B is stratigraphic and ceramic. In Vats's Trench I (HARP Trench 37) a hearth near the bottom of the street deposits gave a calibrated intercept of 2328 BC, from which Meadow and Kenoyer (2000: 324-325) place most intact deposits in the second half of Period 3B and the earliest part of 3C, while allowing that the lowest layers might reach into 3A.

syntheses.statement: Vats dated Mound F Strata I-III (Late I-III) to 'Circa 2750 B.C. to 3050 B.C.', Strata IV-VII (Intermediate I-IV) to 'Circa 3050 B.C. to 3500 B.C.' and Stratum VIII (Early I) to the 'First half of the 4th Millennium B.C.', on the evidence of Marshall's chronology for Mohenjo-daro.
syntheses.disagreement: About a millennium older than HARP: Meadow and Kenoyer (2000: 324-325) correlate Vats's Strata V-VII in Trench I with the second half of Period 3B and the earliest part of 3C, c. 2450-2200 BC and later.

syntheses.statement: Correlating Vats's depths with HARP elevations, 'what we define as Period 3B would lie below about 12 feet and Period 3C material at about 12 feet and above'; 'even if most of the lower deposits of Mound F, Trench I, actually cover all of our Period 3B and the earliest cultural layers extend into Period 3A', the inscribed material is concentrated in the upper part of the sequence.
syntheses.disagreement: Leaves open that the earliest Mound F deposits begin in late 3A, slightly before the 3B settlement described in Meadow and Kenoyer 2005.

syntheses.statement: Wheeler describes the 'granaries' on Mound F as standing 'in orderly array on a carefully-built [platform] with a battered retaining-wall of burnt brick, similar to that which revets the defences of the citadel', with circular working-platforms and 'cooly-quarters' between them and the citadel; he gives no date.

parts.conflicts: Vats (1940: 9) dated the Mound F strata that include the 'granary' levels to c. 3500-2750 B.C. by comparison with Mohenjo-daro; HARP's radiocarbon and ceramics place the settlement, its perimeter wall and the Great Hall in Period 3B (from c. 2450/2400 BC). No Period 3A determination from Mound F has been published; the area was then a clay pit filling with refuse (Meadow and Kenoyer 2005: 211). HARP's fuller account of the Mound F wall (Meadow and Kenoyer 2008, South Asian Archaeology 1999: 85-109) was not available to us.

first_occupation.phase: Period 1, Ravi (aspect of the Hakra) Phase, sub-periods 1A and 1B
first_occupation.basis: HARP's 2010 chart gives Period 1 as 'ca. 3700 BC - ca. 2800 BC' (Kenoyer and Meadow 2010: xlv, xlvii), in calibrated radiocarbon years. The Ravi Phase lies on natural soil on the north side of Mound AB (Trench 39) and at the north-west corner of Mound E (Kenoyer and Meadow 2000: 56, 58). Published determinations from Period 1 include, from Mound AB Trench 39S, WG-2515 4400+/-70 bp (3254 (3028, 2975, 2930) 2915 cal BC; pit 193 on natural soil), WG-2516 4260+/-70 bp, Beta-93760 4320+/-50 bp, Beta-93759 4210+/-50 bp (all 1A) and WG-2518 4980+/-60 bp (3899 (3772) 3698 cal BC, 1B) (Kenoyer and Meadow 2000: 74); and Beta-163719 4480+/-50 bp (3355-3015), Beta-163715 4430+/-40 bp (3330-2920) and Beta-163717 4390+/-40 bp (3100-2900), all 1A (Meadow and Kenoyer 2005: 209). The 2005 paper notes that 'Most of the relevant dates ... are not older than c. 3300 calBC even if one takes the earliest extreme of the 2-sigma calibrated range', while allowing earlier Ravi occupation buried in the centre of Mound AB (p. 209). Wheeler (1947: 59, 66, 93) recorded an earlier 'town- or village-occupation' (layer 26 in HP XXX) below the AB defences, which HARP identifies as Early Harappan (Kot Diji); Vats (1940: 9) dated the lowest stratum of Mound F to the first half of the fourth millennium B.C. by cross-dating.

notes:
Harappa has four large walled mounds, and HARP (the Harappa Archaeological Research Project, Dales and Kenoyer from 1986, Meadow and Kenoyer from 1992) dates their walls to different periods, so we record six parts. Mounds AB and E were each enclosed by a massive mud-brick wall in the Kot Diji Phase (Period 2, c. 2800-2600 BC); on Mound AB and the north-west of Mound E the Harappan-phase walls of Period 3A were built on or just beside those walls, while the southern and eastern wall of Mound E was laid out afresh at the start of Period 3A, in places cutting through Period 2 deposits. Mound ET was walled as an extension of the Mound E circuit after c. 2470 BC (Period 3B in Kenoyer 2008), and Mound F, previously a clay pit, was settled and walled in Period 3B. A further mound under modern Harappa town is unexcavated, and the 'walled suburbs ... to the north and south of Mound AB' of Period 3B (Kenoyer 2008, manuscript p. 13) are documented in our sources only for Mound F.

HARP's period labels changed. The 1988-1991 scheme had Period 1 (Early Harappan, before the north-west revetment walls of Mound E), Period 2 (Transitional) and Period 3 (Harappan); after the Ravi Phase was found on Mound AB in 1996, Period 1 became the Ravi Phase (1A, 1B), the old Mound E Period 1 was reassigned to late 1B, and Period 2 became the Kot Diji Phase (Kenoyer and Meadow 2000: 55-58). We give each determination the phase label its source prints and note the change. The 1997 paper still calls Period 2 'Early Harappan/Harappan Transitional'. HARP's ranges for the start of Period 1 also vary between publications: c. 3300 BC (2000: 55; 2005: 207), 3300 BCE in the chart and >3500 BC in the text of 2001 (meadow2001recent1), >3900 BC (2008 manuscript p. 6), >3700 BC (2011: 5) and ca. 3700 BC (2010: xlv).

All HARP determinations are printed on the 5568-year half-life (stated in the 1991, 1997, 2000 and 2005 tables), so age_bp_5568 copies the printed value; Kenoyer 1991 additionally prints an uncalibrated 'B.C.' value on the 5730-year half-life, which we give in notes. Where the 1997 table prints asymmetric errors we record the larger value and give the printed form in the note. The 2005 table gives lot numbers without trenches; our assignment of its Period 2 dates to Mound AB and of its Period 3A date to Mound E is an inference from the lot numbers in the same paper's figure captions and is marked in each entry.

Determinations left out because they come from later phases and do not date the building of a wall: the Mound E north-west Period 3 series and the Mound E southern-slope Period 3 series of Kenoyer 1991 (p. 43; the stratigraphically earliest southern-slope Period 3 samples, QL-4487 and QL-4488, give CALIB intercepts of 2286 and 2191-2145 BC), the four undivided Mound AB Period 3 dates (WIS-2043, WIS-2144, WIS-2075, WIS-2140), the 1997 Period 3B, 3B/C and 3C/4 series from Trenches 9, 10W, 2 and 31, and the 2005 3B/3C, 3C and Period 5 dates. Kenoyer 1991 lists BETA-33874 (4540+/-180 bp, CALIB 3338, 3213, 3203 BC) under Mound E Period 3; it has the same age and intercepts as the Period 1 sample Beta-33873 and may be a misprint or an old-charcoal sample. None of the Radiocarbon-journal date lists we were given (TF, PRL, PRLC, BS, Penn) contains a determination from Harappa; their 'Harappa culture' entries are from other sites.

We found no published Bayesian model of Harappa's phase boundaries. Possehl's compilations (Radiocarbon Dates for South Asian Archaeology, 1989; Indus Age: The Beginnings, 1999; The Indus Civilization, 2002) and Wright (The Ancient Indus, 2010) were not available in full text (archive.org copies are lending-only), so we cannot report how they treat these dates. HARP's own synthesis Meadow and Kenoyer 2008 (South Asian Archaeology 1999: 85-109), which reports the 1998-1999 work on the Mound AB and Mound F walls, and Meadow and Kenoyer 1994 (South Asian Archaeology 1993: 451-470, 'the city wall and inscribed materials') were not found online. Orientation statements in the sources were not recorded.
